excerpt: Vidyard is a Canadian video platform for sales and marketing teams: screen recording, video messages, AI avatars and hosting. Free plan; Starter from $59/seat/month.
content:
Vidyard is a business video platform from Kitchener, Ontario. Sales, marketing and customer teams use it to record screen and camera videos, send them in email or LinkedIn messages, host videos on websites and see who watched. In recent years it has added AI features: AI avatars that can speak a script in a person's likeness, and a Video Agent add-on that generates personalised videos automatically. Its website also lists video hosting, video hubs and integrations with CRM and marketing automation tools.

The University of Waterloo reports that Michael Litt and Devon Galloway met as systems design engineering undergraduates there and built the company that became Vidyard. In January 2016 Vidyard raised a US$35 million Series C led by Battery Ventures, with existing investor Bessemer Venture Partners taking part. In April 2024 it announced a US$15 million round led by Export Development Canada; BetaKit reported that the round closed the previous summer as an uncapped convertible note and brought total funding to nearly US$91 million.

Pricing

Vidyard's pricing page lists four plans. Free costs nothing and needs no card, with limits such as five videos a month and recordings up to 30 minutes. Starter is US$59 per seat per month billed annually, or US$89 per seat month to month, with unlimited recording, full analytics and a branded sharing page. Teams and Enterprise are custom-priced and billed by invoice, adding CRM integrations, team analytics and SSO. AI video generation needs the Video Agent add-on, priced separately.

Who it suits

Vidyard fits B2B sales and marketing teams that already send a lot of email and want short personal videos with viewing data. Teams who mostly need internal video messages may find simpler tools enough.

We have not tested Vidyard. Prices were checked on its pricing page on 15 October 2026; company history comes from the University of Waterloo, BetaKit and Vidyard's own announcement.
